page: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 7443P processor operating at a base frequency of 2.85 GHz. This system provides 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs via simultaneous multithreading, supported by 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The hardware architecture includes a dedicated CPU allocation with 32 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Local storage consists of a 960 GB solid-state drive, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No graphics processing units are present in this configuration.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong compute capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 10% and multi-core performance in the top 25%. Passmark testing yields a memory score in the top 10%, alongside strong results in CPU encryption, physics, and database operations. In multi-threaded workloads, the server demonstrates strong performance in bzip3 decompression, software compilation with clang, ray tracing, and image processing. Large-block memory bandwidth and text processing benchmarks remain in the average tier. For language model tasks, the system achieves top-tier text generation speeds on small models and strong generation speeds on medium models, though large model inference is unsupported due to memory and hardware constraints.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density and dedicated physical hardware, eliminating virtualization overhead. The combination of high-capacity DDR4 memory and strong multi-core processing makes it a viable option for workloads requiring sustained CPU performance without the noisy-neighbor effects of shared environments. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, database operations, web serving, and moderate-scale text or image processing.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-256gb-amd is a bare metal server powered by an AMD EPYC 7443P processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs. It features 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory, a 960 GB local SSD, and a dedicated CPU allocation. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance and memory scores, alongside strong multi-core capabilities in software compilation, encryption, and physics simulations. While memory bandwidth and text processing perform at average levels, the system delivers strong multi-threaded decompression and efficient small-to-medium language model inference. Lacking a GPU, this server is optimized for non-accelerated, high-density compute tasks. It is highly suited for database operations, software development pipelines, and static web serving where dedicated hardware resources are required to avoid virtualization overhead.
